newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan to probe money-laundering, drugs.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan to probe money-laundering, drugs.

text.p: India and Pakistan signed an agreement on Friday to investigate drug smuggling and money-laundering resulting from one of the world's most lucrative illegal businesses, officials said.

The agreement, signed by Indian Revenue Secretary N.K. Singh, and Pakistan's secretary of the Narcotic Control Board Saeed Ahmed Siddqui, was seen as an important step towards curbing the flow of heroin from Afghanistan into India.

Both countries are also grappling with substantial -- but not firmly quantified -- amounts of illegal money raised from the drug trade, the global value of which is estimated by Interpol at $400 billion.
"We have agreed on what we can do in concert to prevent the menace of drugs from debilitating an entire generation," Singh told reporters after signing the agreement.
India produces surplus quantities of acetic anhydride, a chemical which has various industrial uses but is smuggled in large quantities to Pakistan and used in the processing of poppies into heroin.
U.S. officials have been assisting India in preventing the smuggling of acetic anydride.
Heroin from Pakistan finds its way through its land border into Indian markets from where it is also smuggled abroad, chiefly to Western destinations, officials said.
Friday's agreement was expected to help both countries to set up teams jointly to investigate large-scale drug smuggling and money-laundering, an official statement said.
In one of its biggest drug hauls in 1995, Indian border guards seized 77 kg of heroin, estimated at the time to be worth $22 million on the street.

India is the main supplier of legal opium to the United States. But U.S. officials say their government has been under pressure to cut down imports because of allegations of large-scale diversion of the opium crop into heroin processing.

Indian officials say they have confiscated around 400 kg of heroin annually in recent years, much of it originating within the Afghanistan-based Golden Crescent and the Golden Triangle borders of Laos, Burma and Thailand.
India says its main flow of heroin imports come from the Pakistan-Afghanistan area.
Unofficial estimates say India's black economy, based largely on gold smuggling, tax evasion and in recent years the drug trade, forms 60 percent of national output.
